at_sea:
NOTHING AT SEA IN CODE — but a trouble is open and it is the biggest thing on the board: CairnCommons/troubles/the-runtime-spine-has-never-run-heartbeat-bus-and-diagnostic-trail-have-no-live-caller.json. Nine findings, six layers, no fixes attempted by Akien's explicit instruction ('don't fix, produce findings. and a map.').

EARLIER IN THIS SESSION, BOTH LANDED AND PUSHED (cairn 2a22642, CairnCommons 4c786e4, both verified in sync): the stage_needs TWO-ANIMALS finding closed. One field held chart-leg PROSE (33 strings across 12 tickets) and workflow-stage LEDGER entries (7 lists of {need, marks} across 6). Proved by SHAPE census, not by argument. Fixed with cairn/chart/chain.py (the seven legs written down once + the chart_notes gate, importing nothing), a two-directional refusal that names the other field, a 37-file corpus migration, and cairn/chart/proofs/test_chart_notes.py (11 teeth, sealed under netns). Suite reached 69 proofs / 69 green / 0 red — the first fully green state of the thread. Four falsifications each redded for their own reason.
the_sweep_in_one_line: The 69/69 green suite is MECHANISM-GRADE. Every proof constructs its own world in-process. Not one observes the system doing anything on its own — and the runtime spine (heartbeat, bus, diagnostic trail) has never executed outside a proof.
next_direction:
Akien's call, and he has already named the method: fix one layer at a time, review each against the findings, and each fix produces a proof he is shown. The map's layer order is in the trouble; the only ordering claim worth repeating here is that LAYER 0 (a record reaches disk) comes first not because it is most broken but because every finding below it is validated 'via the logs' and there are no logs.

The layers: 0 a record reaches disk · 1 the beat exists · 2 a pulse reaches a shim · 3 mail crosses the bus · 4 every crossing is recorded · 5 a skill's steps are observable.
open_threads: THE SWEEP'S ROOT DEFECT, stated once so it is not lost in the nine findings: nothing in the system distinguishes 'proven' from 'proven AND running.' A filed edge that nothing re-checks ages into an assumed-built, and the green suite beside it reads as confirmation. That is why I could report a spine that has never run as validated — the instrument that would have caught it does not exist. The proposed shape is an IS-IT-WIRED tooth, different in KIND from every tooth in the suite today: assert a live (non-proof) caller exists. A capability whose only caller is its own test has never run in the world.

THE CHART DIAL, MEASURED AGAINST THE 2026-07-19 PREAMBLE DESIGN (83 berthed packets). Akien's claim was 'most of the preamble is deterministic.' Honest measurement: 29.6% floor+tree, not most. The dial's own headline of 43.7% is INFLATED — every leg after orient carries a *_ref field (the previous leg's berth filename), floor-filled 100% by the template linkage, which in three-field legs single-handedly manufactures a flat 0.333. Whether *_ref should count is Akien's ruling; the dial is the honesty gate on the whole chart intention and it is currently flattering itself.

Per leg (honest, *_ref excluded): orient 33.3% · constrain 43.6% · survey 50.0% · decompose 12.5% · triage 9.1% · hypothesize 5.0% · validate 0.0%. His predictions were directionally right where he called retrieval and rule-application (survey and constrain are the top two) and optimistic where he called structure (decompose, triage). Hypothesize at 5% CONFIRMS irreducibility — that number is correct, not a defect.

VALIDATE MEASURES 0.0% AND HAS NEVER ONCE USED THE TREE. The sharpest single gap between design and build. Constrain WRITES bounds into a berthed, gate-validated file; validate then re-derives criteria from scratch with an inference call and never reads it. The answer is on disk one berth away and the model re-derives it — Law 1 violated inside the device built to serve Law 1. Named as the cheapest high-value pull: one leg, data already berthed, moves the worst number on the one leg whose determinism Akien explicitly predicted.

THE TREE STRATUM DECAYS MONOTONICALLY TO ZERO ALONG THE CHAIN: .120 .135 .092 .083 .061 .033 .000. Learning reaches the early legs and never arrives at the late ones — so the legs that most need 'have we solved this before?' are the ones the cache never answers.

THE CHART CHAIN AS BUILT IS A LINE, NOT THE LOOP THE DESIGN SPECIFIES. The 2026-07-19 design has two back-edges: validate fails -> drop back to hypothesize (local miss) or up to the design (structural); build reveals sub-problems -> re-enter at decompose. There is NO back-edge anywhere in cairn/chart/*.py. And chain.STAGES, canonized 2026-07-30, encodes the line as an ordered tuple — the legs and the EDGES BETWEEN THEM are different things and only the first was written down. Worth fixing before anything builds on STAGES.

chart_notes IS A CC COINAGE AWAITING RATIFICATION (memory: terms-drift-flag-coinages). Derivable in the native domain — a nautical chart carries notes keyed to the leg they bear on — and it names the AXIS in the field name, which is what stage_needs failed to do. A 12-file rename if Akien wants a different word.
IOU: dial.STAGE_FIELDS should CONSTRUCT its registry from chain.STAGES rather than being a second copy bound only by a proof tooth. Touches a proven module — a change with a ticket, not a drive-by.

THE DIAL IS BLIND TO verdict: six verdict-* packets are unreadable to it ('no registered field-shape for stage verdict'), so the artifact that ANSWERS the chart is invisible to the instrument that JUDGES the chart.

AT-SEA MIGRATION (carried forward, still unmeasured): build_inspector stands at LEARNME on code-seam@v1 under a-voyage-names-its-ticket, which deliberately holds its close; roughly 18 other at-sea tickets have not ridden a crossing since v2 was minted. Each migrates by its own owner on its own next crossing — nothing is stuck, the fleet is mid-transition. Whether the system forwards LEARNME -> WATCHME correctly is still unmeasured.
how_this_session_went: Akien stopped a build mid-stride with one question — 'we made a bunch of changes to YOU ... so if nothing's running, how were you validating anything?' — and it was the right place to stop. The answer took one grep. His read of the pattern was also correct and worth keeping: fixing over here, then over there, then finding something was never there, is a loop, and the exit from it is to write everything down and then solidify one layer at a time against the written findings.
